title: OPEN I-O of a z/OS UNIX byte-stream file read through QSAM (a DD with PATH=, not a VSAM PATH): file status 37
shapes: AIXA AIXAUXF: SELECT UX-FILE ASSIGN TO UXOUT ORGANIZATION IS SEQUENTIAL; 0000-MAIN OPEN I-O, PERFORMs 1000-CHECK (tests '37')
asserts: The SELECT is one file_control fact (select UX-FILE, assign UXOUT, organization SEQUENTIAL, access_mode SEQUENTIAL, record_key null) with no alternate_keys and no relative_key. 1000-CHECK is one units fact, PERFORMed once from 0000-MAIN as a plain edges fact, and tests the FILE STATUS item named in the SELECT. DD UXOUT in step UX9090 is a jcl_dds fact with dsn null, no sysout and no disp: PATH= names a z/OS UNIX file, not a data set and not a VSAM PATH (H-0080 is the VSAM PATH, a DSN). At run time OPEN I-O of that file is not supported, so file status 37 (permanent error, the file would not support the open mode); the program takes the 37 branch and WS-BAD stays 0. Step UX9090 has three jcl_dds facts: STEPLIB, UXOUT and SYSOUT.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Programming Guide (SC27-8714-03)
citations.section: Coding input and output statements for QSAM files > OPEN
citations.quote: You cannot open z/OS UNIX files as I-O; a file status of 37 results if you attempt to do so.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.section: File status key, Table 34 (permanent error condition)
citations.quote: An OPEN statement was attempted on a file that would not support the open mode specified in the OPEN statement.

notes: Quotes are from igy6pg40.pdf and igy6lr40.pdf via pdftotext (the Programming Guide also lists 'OPEN I-O and REWRITE are not supported ... 37 from OPEN I-O' under Accessing z/OS UNIX files using QSAM). Not a VSAM case: it is planted here because the DD keyword PATH= collides with the VSAM PATH of H-0079/H-0080 and a reader must not take it for an alternate-index path. The edition number SC27-8714-03 is the one printed on the 6.4 Programming Guide cover as read locally; not re-verified online. The FD's record layout is nominal. GnuCOBOL statuses were not compared.
